messages:
ana-peopleops: Hey team — new hire Lina (EAD pending) asked about medical vaccine exemption docs for onboarding. She needs to confirm what we accept for I-9 / benefits enrollment and any visa/EAD evidence we should forward to the immigration team.

matt-peopleops: Short answer: we can accept a medical exemption letter for internal benefits + I-9 if it meets our doc checklist, but for immigration/EAD purposes we may need additional evidence. @raj-immigration can you confirm what USCIS/consulate typically accepts?

raj-immigration: For immigration filings we don't want to guess legal standards here, but practically we ask hires to provide: (1) a signed medical provider letter stating the medical contraindication, (2) date of exam, (3) provider name and license, (4) a clear link to the clinic name/contact. If docs are foreign, include an English translation + translator attestation. We'll escalate if the consulate requests specific proof. :white_check_mark:

lina-newhire: Thanks — can you confirm whether a clinic appointment confirmation email + a doctor note is OK? My primary care said they can write a note but they'd only note "medical exemption" without a license number on the first draft.

ana-peopleops: Clinic confirmation + doctor note is fine as long as the doctor note is legible and includes provider details. If license number is missing, ask the clinic to add name and clinic contact info so we can verify if needed. Deadline: please upload to our secure HR portal by EOD Friday so benefits team can finish enrollment.

matt-peopleops: For I-9: remember we still need acceptable identity and employment authorization docs (EAD card, passport, etc.). The medical exemption doesn’t replace identity docs. Lina — do you have the copy of your EAD or receipt notice? If only receipt, we can use that for the 90-day workaround per our policy; ping me privately.

lina-newhire: I have the EAD receipt (I-797C) and passport. I'll upload both. Is a scanned PDF OK or do you need originals in person?

ana-peopleops: Scanned PDFs uploaded to the secure portal are OK for now; we'll schedule a quick in-person or video verification for originals within 3 days of start if EAD is still pending. We'll note the exception in the file. :calendar:

raj-immigration: One more thing — if the hire plans to travel for consular stamping while exemption is claimed, consulates vary widely. Advise them to carry the full medical documentation and translations. We can draft a short summary letter for Lina to carry if needed.

lina-newhire: Appreciate it. Would be super helpful to have that summary letter — thanks.

ana-peopleops: I'll draft the summary and post the template here. In the meantime: Lina, upload the doctor's letter (with clinic contact) + EAD receipt + passport scan. @imm-bot will ping when upload completes.

imm-bot: Reminder set: "Check Lina uploads" in 48h. :robot_face:

matt-peopleops: Also tagging benefits team: benefits@redwood.com — once docs are in we'll process enrollment and retro dates. If medical exemption affects dependent coverage, benefits will reach out separately.

ana-peopleops: Perfect — thanks all. Lina, lmk when you upload and we’ll move forward with benefits + immigration note. :sparkles:
